0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian
Standard ( Second Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 31 October 1980, after the draft finalized by the Building Construction Practices Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council. 0.2 Mud PHLJSX,4 is a common type of insulating course in the roof used in hot dry regions of the country, such as in the states of Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and other regions where the rainfall is not heavy. 1~s reasonably durable and adds enough therma insulation fol use is cheap, maintaining relatively comfortable temperature in the interior. In laying the roof, however, there. are several important details of workmanship which, if neglected, will considerably reduce the efficacy of the roof. This standard is intended to serve as a guide in the work of laying mud PHUSk`A in flat roofs. 0.3 This standard was first published in 1962 and subsequently revised The present revision has been taken up to incorporate the in 1967. improvements found necessary during usage of the standard and in the light of comments and suggestions received from various organizations. In this revision, the requirement of soil for the preparation of lnuti PHlJSKA and tiud plaster has been modified SO that a reasonable The binding and reinforcing ingredients cohesive soil could be obtained. which are actually used in practice for the preparation of mud plastel has been spelt out and the method of preparation of `Iceping' plaster has The revision also specifies the minimum compacted been dealt in detail. thickness of PHUSKA.

0.4 For the purpose

of deciding whether a particular requirement of tllis standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, exprcssing the resuIt of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance The number of significant places retained in th(: with IS : 2-1960*. rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

3.3 Arrangements shall also be made for the proper exchange of information amongst all, concerned with the execution of the roofing work to ensure proper co-ordination. 4. DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS Against Water Penetration

4.1 Protection

4.1.1 Mud PHUSKA layer by itself niay not be sufficiently waterproof for the roof and it may be necessary to provide beneath it a waterproofing layer or membrane to be effective in this respect. Care shall also be exercised while doing the roof finish work to compact the mud PHUSKA layer to the maximum density ( SCB8.1 ). 4.1.2 The slope of the terrace shall be such as to drain off promptly all rain-water falling on the roof surface well before the water begins to seep through cracks, if any, into the mud PHUSKA layer. The slope If it is not possible to give all the slope by shall not be less than 1 in 40. the mud PHUSKA layer, part of the slope required for roof drainage may be given in the sub-floor itself. 4.1.3 Rain-water pipes to be provided for roof drainage shall be determined in accordance with the intensity and duration of the rainfall in the area. The cross-sectional area of flow of the rain-water pipe shall be not less than l/5000 of the roof area drained, and the pipe shall in no case be less than 100 mm diameter. 4.2 Durability-Mud PHUSKA will be suitable in hot dry regions where the rainfall is not heavy and extremely hot temperature occur during the sumnler. The durabilitv of the mud PHUSKA layer depends on how the protcctivi: surface, nameiy, the mud plaster or the brick tiles free of cracks. When the layer as the case may bc, are maintained cracks develop in the mud plaster, <jr wilen the joints of brick tile layer get dislodged, water will find its way to the,mud PHUSKA layer through Regular maintenance is necessary to fill up cracks so as to seepage. extend the life of the finish. 4..2.1 In areas where there is no rainfall and there is very little variation in temperature, and where clay of good quality is used for mud PHUSKA paving with tiles may not be necessary over the mud PHUSKA Paving finish lvill, however, be ne cessary where the roof is used layer. for living and sl;+ng purposes and also if additional durability and thermal insulation is rcqkiirr:;. 5. MATERIAL 5.1 Soil for Mud PHUSKA - The from gravel and coarse sand (of 5 soil for mud PHUSKA shall be free particle size greater than 2 mm ),

vegetable matter and fine KA.j%4R particles. The coarse material shall not exceed 25 percent by mass. The soil shall also be free from harmful and efflorescent salts. The plasticity index of the soil shall be between 10 to 15 percent.
NOTE 1 -Generally soil suitable for brick making is suitable for mud PHUSKA from localities afflicted by white ants may not be cohesive soil.

The above plasticity index will indicate a reasonable

5.2 Soil for Mud Plaster and Mud Mortar-The soil shall be free from vegetable roots, gravel and coarse sand of particle size greater than 2 mm. The coarse material shall not exceed 10 percent by mass. The soil shall also be free from harmful and efflorescent salts. The plasticity index of the soil shall be between 10 to 15 percent. 5.3 Mud Plaster-The mud plaster shall be prepared from soil conforming to 5.2. The dry soil shall be reduced to fine powder and mixed with water in a pit, adding wheat straw 6 percent by mass and cowdung 12 percent by mass. The mixture shall be allowed to rot for a period of During this period, it shall be pugged manually not less than 7 days. using spades if necessary to get a homogeneous mass free from lumps and clods.
NOTE - The wheat straw used may be of any size since it would be broken to small size during the rotting period.

.

5.3.1 The consistency of the mortar shall be adjusted by taking it in a trowel and observing how it slides off the face of the trowel. The mortar shall readily slide off, but at the same time shall not be so wet as to part Alternatively, slump test may be into large drops before falling. performed in accordance with the procedure laid down in IS: 1IL@-1959*. The slump should be about 70 mm. 5.4 Cut-Back. adding 20 parts 80/100 bitumen a homogeneous Bitumen - Cut-back bitumen shall be prepared by of kerosene oil and 1 part of paraffin wax to 80 parts of The mixture shall be worked to melted on gentle fire. mass.

5.5 Mud Mortar C Mud mortar used as bedding under brick tile layer ( see 5.3 ) but shall be prepared in the same manner as mud plaster without any addition of fibrous reinforcing material and binding,material. The mud mortar may be used immediately without any rotting period. 5.5.1 The mortar shall be mixed with 2 percent of bitumen cut back ( see 5.4 ) by mass of dry soil and worked to a homogeneous mass.

5.11 Cement Mortar for Grouting - Cement mortar for grouting shall consist of one part of cement and three parts of sand by volume 01 any richer mortar as may be required in special circumstances. The mortar shall be prepared as laid down in IS : 2250 - 1965-i-t. Wherever ordinary cement is used, it will be preferable to add burnt clay pozzolana in suitable proportions depending upon its pozzolanic activity. 6. 6.3 Before the finishing work is started, all points of level for the finished Wherever slopes in finished floors are roof surface shall be marked out. desired, points of level and outlets shall be correctly marked and outlet openings made beforehand. 6.4 Protection Against Dampness -Wherever it is feared or suspected that moisture may percolate to the top of the sub-floor during any time of the year, the same shall be treated as explained in the relevant Indian Standards on waterproofing and damp-proofing to prevent such conditions. Where water is likely to percolate from the side walls, the roof surface shall also be properly waterproofed against the wall up to a level of at least 150 mm above the sub-floor. *Specification for burnt clay flat terracing tiles : Part I Machine made (@t revirio~l ). tSpecification for burnt clay flat terracing tiles : Part II Hand made (first reotiion ) . #Specification for ordinary and low heat Portland cement ( ihlrd revtiion). �Specilication for portland slag cement ( Ukdretiion). 7. LAYING

OF MUD PHUSKA

- `I`he soil as defined in 5.1 :.hall be stacked in required quantities in zl)out 300 mm high stacks over a level ground and the top surface divic!cxc! into suitable compartments of convenient size by bunding. The estimated quantity of water corresponding to optimum moisture content shall be added about 12 hours before the use and The stacks of soil shall then be worked up with spades allowed to soak. and hands to ensure proper distribution of moisture at the time the soil is to be used, 7.1 Preparation
Nova - Generally soil of this type will rcquirc aq optimum moisture of about 1451/m3. A practical way of determining tht: moisture content of soil suitable for giving good compaction is that th? soil should contain that much quantity of fi oislur `, which .wh~ n ;L handful of soil is moulded with hand to the shapeof a ball. ir shall just r:tain its form. If thr soil on moulding cannot retain its shape of a ball, moistllrr contrnt is inadrquate. On the other hand, if the ball can be p!asticall\- deformed on pressing with hand, the moisture content is on the hight,r ski:..

7.2 iaaying - The mud PHlJSZC,l prepared as in 7.1 shall be carried to the surface to be coveretl and laid in loose thickness not greater than 150 mm. The surface shnll then be brought to the proper slope. It sh;!ll then be ramt:lcd manually with wooden rammers and THAPPIES so as to obtain n::\ximum density. Normally a mud PHUSXA layer laid to a compacted thickness of not less than 100 mm is considered adequate. 7.3 The surface shall be allowed to dry for a period of not less than 24 If any cracks appear, these shall be filled with a grout of the krzz& material that is used in the LEEPING ( usually GOHRI ).

8. APPLYING

MUD PLASTER

8.1 After laying the mud PHUSXA, mud plaster prepared as specified in 5.3 shall be laid to a total thickness of not less than 25 mm over the The plaster may be applied in a single coat or two coats of surface. 15 mm and 10 mm, the latter being preferable. After the application, the coat of plaster shall be allowed to dry. If any hair cracks open out The surface shall be checked they shall be filled with a grout as in 7.3. once more for slope and evenness with a straight edge and spirit-level and made up wherever necessary by application of the plaster.
8.2 When the surface of the mud plaster coating has dried a thin coat of LEEPIflG plaster as specified in 5.6 shall be applied to a thickness of not less than 3 mm. The surface shall be allowed to dry. When hair cracks appear they shall be filled as described in 7.3. The LEEPING shall be finished with the trowel OT float. 8

IS : 2115 - 19fJO 9. PAVING WITH BRICK-TILES 9.0 This paving finish will be necessary
where the roof is used for living and sleeping purposes and also if additional durability and thermal insulation is required. Tiled paving finish shall be laid down directly over the mud plaster and no LEEPlfiC will be necessary.

9.1 The brick tiles shall be laid flat on a thin layer of mud mortar.

The The mud mortar shall be used mud mortar shall be as specified in.5.5. to the minimum extent to give a level surface. The tiles shall be laid close to each other and the thickness of joints shall not be less than 6 mm It shall be ensured while laying the tiles and not more than 15 mm. that the mud mortar rises vertically in the joints to a height of about The brick-tile work shall be allowed to dry for a period of 24 15 mm. Care shall be taken at the time of hours before grouting of the joints. grouting the joints not to displace the tiles laid in position on the roof finish. 9.2 When the brick-tile work has dried, the joints shall be grouted wit11 It shall be ensured that the joints are cement-sand mortar as in 5.10.
